title: Terraform primitive modules playbook (VPC/IAM/Cluster) - draft
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook for our primitive Terraform modules for private deployments. Focus is on: VPC networking primitives, IAM role/policy primitives, and cluster primitives (EKS/GKE/AKS). Goal: produce small, composable modules that are safe to upgrade in live Dedicated/Private environments and that can be composed into higher-level stacks by Solutions/Platform teams.

High-level design principles (quick):
- Single responsibility: each module manages one primary resource type (vpc, subnet, route-table, igw/natgw, iam-role, iam-policy, cluster-control-plane, node-pool).
- Stable inputs (compatibility): public inputs are stable; add new optional inputs rather than changing semantics of existing ones.
- Outputs are minimal and explicit; avoid exporting provider internals when not needed.
- Backwards-compatible defaults: preserve existing behavior unless explicitly bumped major version.
- Idempotent and safe to re-run in CI and during in-place upgrades.

Module naming and repository layout (proposal):
- infra-modules/network/v1 (vpc, subnet, route_table, nat, egress)
- infra-modules/iam/v1 (role, policy, instance_profile)
- infra-modules/cluster/eks/v1 (control_plane, node_pool, addon-helm)
- infra-modules/cluster/gke/v1 (control_plane, node_pool, addon-config)
- infra-modules/cluster/aks/v1 (control_plane, node_pool)
Each module directory contains: README.md, examples/, variables.tf (documented), outputs.tf, main.tf, tests/ (terragrunt or kitchen-terraform short tests), CHANGELOG.md

Recommended variables pattern (public API):
- Keep variable names flat and prefixed by module shortname when ambiguous, e.g., vpc_cidr, subnet_private_cidrs (list), cluster_name, node_pool_instance_types (list).
- Avoid complex maps as primary inputs unless needed; maps are harder to evolve. Use lists of objects with documented index semantics for node pools.
- Mark secrets as sensitive = true and expect values to be provided from vault or Terraform Cloud variables in production.

Example variable list (cluster/node-pool module):
- cluster_name (string) - required
- k8s_version (string) - default = "1.27"
- control_plane_instance_type (string) - default depends on provider
- node_pools (list) - each entry: { name, min_size, max_size, desired_size, instance_type, taints, labels }
- vpc_id (string) - optional (attach to existing)
- subnet_ids (list) - optional (prefer passing explicit if private VPC exists)
- service_account_roles (map) - optional: well-known service accounts -> iam role arn
- enable_managed_node_groups (bool) - default = false (explicit opt-in)

Recommended outputs (examples):
- vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, nat_gateway_ids
- iam_role_arn, iam_policy_arn
- cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_cert, cluster_oidc_provider_arn (if created)
- kubeconfig_cert (sensitive) - avoid serializing large certs unless necessary; better to surface cluster endpoint + data needed for in-cluster auth.

EKS vs GKE vs AKS: primitives checklist
- Common: cluster_name, network integration hooks, node pools, node labels/taints, control plane versioning, addons (CNI, metrics, ingress)
- EKS-specific: OIDC provider creation (for IRSA), eksctl vs aws_eks_cluster choices, AMI/launch template handling, kubelet bootstrap args
- GKE-specific: enable_shielded_nodes, node_pools autoscaling settings, workload_identity config
- AKS-specific: managed_identity_integration, AAD profiles, azure_cni vs kubenet
Make module differences explicit in README and examples folder.

Upgrade/migration playbook (high level):
1) Pre-upgrade validation (CI + manual):
   - Run terraform plan on a staging account with the new module pinned locally.
   - Static checks: tfsec, checkov, custom lint rules for forbidden changes (e.g., replacing subnet CIDR).
   - Validate provider version constraints and ensure providers are pinned in root modules.
2) API/behavior compatibility matrix:
   - For each variable that changed semantics, add an opt-in flag (e.g., new_node_pool_flow = true). Never silently flip behavior on default.
3) State migration steps (when renaming resources or refactoring):
   - Document exact terraform state mv commands in the PR and keep them in migration/ in repo. Example: terraform state mv module.old.node_group.aws_eks_node_group.module.new_node_group[0]
   - For lifecycle-replace operations, provide a blue-green strategy: create new resource, cordon/drain workloads, switch traffic, destroy old resource.
4) Rolling upgrade constraints for clusters:
   - Node pools: prefer create new node pool and migrate workloads vs in-place replace where possible.
   - Ensure PDBs and PodDisruptionBudgets are installed and respected during drain.
5) Rollback plan:
   - Keep old tfstate snapshot and module pin for a quick revert.
   - Provide a revert runbook: terraform apply with old module version and state restored from snapshot; if node pool replaced, recreate old pool and reattach workloads.

On-prem / air-gapped considerations:
- Providers: some providers require network egress (GCR, Helm registries). Use private helm registries or OCI caches. Document required firewall rules in module README.
- Image provisioning: prefer node-pool bootstrap scripts that pull from internal registries. Provide example for kubelet extra args and registry mirrors.
- CNI: Calico/Weave/Other - choose a default that works well offline; keep addon module flexible to accept a pre-bundled manifest.

IAM primitives & least-privilege guidance:
- Modules should produce minimal role/policy documents and allow policy extension via additional_policy_arns input (list).
- Prefer templates that accept a list of allowed actions instead of big managed-policies; provide curated managed policies in infra repo.
- Output role_arn and role_name only; avoid returning policy document JSON unless necessary.

Testing and CI:
- Per-module unit tests using terraform init/plan with local backend plus acceptance tests in a sandbox cloud account.
- Terraform fmt & validate as gate. tfsec + checkov in PR pipeline.
- Example CI matrix: provider versions (latest patch), tf version matrix (1.4.x - 1.6.x), run plans for default + example inputs.

Versioning policy and CHANGELOGs:
- Follow semantic versioning for modules. Minor/patch releases should preserve input/output names. Major bump required if any input/output/semantic-breaking change.
- Tag releases in git and publish registry entries (internal registry).

Examples of sensitive transitions we must avoid or handle with care:
- Changing subnet CIDR or replacing a subnet resource => plan will show replacement. Instead we should add support for dual-stack or additional subnets and migrate resources.
- Renaming resource addresses in module interface (forces state mv). If unavoidable, include safe state migration steps in PR and automate via release script.

Operator playbook snippet (for on-call or migration lead):
- Step 0: Inform stakeholders and open migration ticket, include rollback owners and expected outage window.
- Step 1: Run preflight script: ./scripts/preflight-checks.sh --cluster <name> (checks PDBs, node readiness, service endpoints, quotas)
- Step 2: Apply module in staging and verify workloads boot correctly.
- Step 3: Apply to a single zone/region small workload first, then proceed to critical clusters.
- Step 4: Monitor metrics (pod restarts, scheduler latency, auth errors) for 60m post-change.
- Step 5: If failure, run revert.sh (automated) which restores old tfstate snapshot and re-applies pinned module version.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide canonical shape for node_pools input (map vs list of objects). Preference: list-of-objects with explicit name field.
- Agree default Kubernetes versions per provider and how long we support older defaults in module.
- Standardize tagging/labeling scheme across modules (cost center, owner, env).
- Add module-level telemetry hooks (optional) for usage tracking in Dedicated accounts (privacy review needed).

Appendix: short example (pseudo-terraform usage)
module "vpc" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/network/v1//vpc"
  vpc_cidr = "10.10.0.0/16"
  public_subnet_suffixes = ["a","b"]
}
module "eks_cluster" {
  source = "github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/cluster/eks/v1//control_plane"
  cluster_name = "corp-dedicated-prod-eu"
  k8s_version = "1.27"
  vpc_id = module.vpc.vpc_id
  subnet_ids = module.vpc.private_subnet_ids
  node_pools = [
    { name = "app", min_size = 2, max_size = 6, desired_size = 3, instance_type = "m6i.large" }
  ]
}

Contact/ownership:
- Primary author: Priya Shah (eng-private-deployments)
- Reviewer: Marcus Lee (platform-engineering), Ana Rodriguez (serving-runtime)

Next steps (short):
- Iterate on node_pools schema and land RFC in repo by end of Q1 2026.
- Add migration scripts for the two outstanding forks where we changed resource addresses in prod.
- Draft module template with detailed README and example for each provider.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc intentionally pragmatic and example-driven; migrate long-form policy guidance to Confluence once design stabilizes.
